summary: Scope is where in the code a variable can be used. A variable made with let or const exists only from its declaration to the closing brace of its block.
notes: message is declared inside the if braces, so it is gone after the closing brace. status is declared before the if, so it still exists after it.
var quiz is still there after the loop. It is 4, because the loop stops when quiz <= 3 becomes false.
addPoints() changes the outer totalPoints directly. reset() declares its own totalPoints with let, so the outer one stays 25.
pitfall: Using a let variable above its declaration in the same block causes ReferenceError: Cannot access 'status' before initialization.
contrast: JavaScript's let and const live only inside their braces, like Java. The older var ignores if and loop braces, like a Python variable. A function can change an outer variable without Python's global keyword.
